thread: Follow the sky upward: begin with weather watched from a hill, travel through the instrumented atmosphere, and end among telescopes listening to the stars. Each stop gives the swarm new sensors, signals, and celestial neighbors to become.

candidates.name: Blue Hill Observatory and Science Center
candidates.why: A hilltop weather station with historic instruments, daily observations, climate archives, and long-running records: sunshine recorders and wind gauges can become patient, weather-sensitive creatures.

candidates.name: Earth Observing Laboratory
candidates.why: Research aircraft, airborne instruments, ground-based radars, and field campaigns offer a menagerie of flying samplers and cloud-probing machines.

candidates.name: National Observatory of Athens
candidates.why: The observatory connects atmospheric sensing and meteorological networks with mountaintop telescopes and historical scientific instruments, making a natural bridge from air to space.

candidates.name: Perth Observatory
candidates.why: Southern-sky telescopes, research projects, a historical instrument museum, and even tiny fairy doors suggest both astronomical and miniature inhabitants.

candidates.name: National Solar Observatory
candidates.why: Solar telescopes, magnetic fields, sunspots, and instruments built to study the Sun provide material for bright, turbulent creatures.

candidates.name: National Radio Astronomy Observatory
candidates.why: Radio dishes, interferometer arrays, cosmic molecules, and invisible radio signals invite creatures that listen across enormous distances.

candidates.name: Hungarian Meteorological Service
candidates.why: Forecast models, radar, lake observations, climate records, and a meteorological museum full of old measuring devices offer many ways to sense the lower sky.

candidates.name: European Southern Observatory
candidates.why: Desert observatories, giant segmented mirrors, instruments, and images of distant nebulae give the journey a deep-space ending.
